title: The 3 Best Juicers for Hard Vegetables
h1: The 3 Best Juicers for Hard Vegetables
metaDescription: Our 3 picks for juicers for hard vegetables, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at juicers for hard vegetables using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Omega J8006HDS Masticating Juicer
products.blurb: Key specs: 80 RPM dual-stage auger, 200W motor, 37oz juice container.
strengths: Dual-stage auger crushes dense root vegetables thoroughly rather than shredding around them
Reverse switch clears jams from tough, fibrous ginger without disassembly
15-year warranty reflects a build designed for sustained heavy-produce use
limitations: Slower processing pace than a high-wattage centrifugal juicer
Beets and carrots should be cut into smaller chunks first for the narrower chute
Small pulp bin fills up fast on a big batch of dense root vegetables

products.name: Breville Juice Fountain Cold
products.blurb: Key specs: 850W motor, Cold Spin Technology, 70oz juice jug.
strengths: 850W motor spins through carrots and beets quickly without stalling
Wide feed chute takes whole or roughly chopped carrots with minimal prep
Large 70oz jug handles a bigger batch of dense vegetables before needing to empty
limitations: Somewhat more pulp waste on dense root vegetables than a masticating juicer
Louder motor under the load of hard produce
Higher power draw than the masticating options here

products.name: Hurom H-AA Slow Juicer
products.blurb: Key specs: Single auger, upright design, 150W quiet motor, Adjustable pulp control lever.
strengths: Adjustable pulp lever helps fine-tune output on fibrous root vegetables
Quiet motor even when working through dense produce
limitations: Most expensive option on this list
Narrower feed chamber requires more pre-cutting of large beets and carrots
Lower wattage than the Breville, which can mean a slower pace on big batches

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
